Well there's several safeguards in place to make sure that the organs are distributed fairly. There's pediatric priority so kids get first dibs. Then you have size of organs, as obviously an adult liver won't fit in a 6 month old with biliary atresia. Age of organ donor and age of recipient are considered as well. So an organ from someone in their 70s won't end up in a little kid. Healthy BMI is required, and in cases of alcoholic cirrhosis, you have to be sober for a year before they'll consider listing you. You're given a score that indicates how sick you are. In the case of livers, its called PELD score for kids (pediatric end stage liver disease) and for adults it's a MELD score (model for end stage liver disease) The higher your score, the higher on the list you are. It has 0 (no liver disease) but ranges from 5-40. 5 is low, but 40 means you won't survive 24 hours without transplantation. Sometimes people are given a score as high as 42 if they won't survive the night. Usually once you hit those numbers though you're too sick to be transplanted and so you're put on palliative care. My MELD never got very high, only 14. Unfortunately the MELD system doesn't factor in two of the worst comorbidities; esophageal varices due to portal hypertension, and hepatic encephalopathy. I had both so if those were factored in my score I would've been in the mid 30s at the lowest.
